content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: service level is predicted to recover to 99.2% for 13:45-15:45, well above the 80% target.","why":"The 10:30 spike in payments calls (213 against 111.9 forecast, service level down to 4.7%, 59 abandoned) traces to the P1 UPI switch incident INC-20261006-6998. Upi_payment_failed calls were 2.56x normal over the last four intervals. Staffing is at plan (42 of 43), handle time is below forecast, and there are no campaigns. For the disruption window 13:45-15:45, the forecast with no changes is 99.2% overall, with payments at 98.5% and general at 100%. Predicted abandonment is 0.2%, and rest-of-day service level is 99.4%. The target is met at zero cost without any intervention.","trade_offs":["IVR callbacks on general (P1) or on both queues (P3) cost nothing but give the same predicted 99.2%, so they only add customer-facing changes for no gain.","Lending one cross-skilled agent from payments to general (P2) lowers payments to 98.1% and the overall figure to 98.9% while general stays at 100%. It adds risk to the queue hit by the outage for no benefit."],"watch":"The forecast assumes the UPI outage effect continues to fade. If the incident stays open or payments volume or abandons rise again, revisit the plan. P3's callback cover on both queues is a ready no-cost fallback."}
